crm_note.headline: Chloe debriefed after Brackenvane second round (mental maths test, market-making game, betting game, options questions); awaiting feedback
crm_note.how_it_went: Chloe said it was the most fun she has had in an interview and also the most stressed. She got through about seventy of eighty mental maths questions and felt that was slow. In the market-making game Sam approved of her widening, but she got her position wrong by one lot. She thinks she was too cautious in the betting game, and she was comfortable on the options questions.

rounds.format: Tablet test before the game, eighty questions in eight minutes
asked: Fractions, decimals and a few percentages
rounds.candidate_view: Got through about seventy, with no idea how many were right. She said seventy out of eighty felt slow and is worried she is too slow at the maths for them.

rounds.format: About an hour with two traders from the index options desk, Sam and Bea
asked: Make a market on the sum of three dice, with dice revealed one at a time while they traded against her
Sam asked why she had widened
Bea asked what her position was
rounds.candidate_view: She quoted 9.5 at 11.5 around a fair value of 10.5, moved her mid to 13 after a six, and widened when they lifted her and seemed to have information. Sam said good, as many people keep quoting tight to look confident. She got her position wrong by one lot, which annoyed her, and Bea told her firmly to always know her position.

rounds.format: Offered bets at different odds and asked to decide sizing
rounds.candidate_view: She thinks she was too cautious and was sizing small. She knew Kelly but did not use it properly.

rounds.format: Questions at the end of the session
asked: What happens to a call's delta as expiry gets close
Why an index skew exists at all
rounds.candidate_view: Comfortable with this part, as it is her day job at Kelmscroft.

compensation.expectation: Base around £110k, with a bonus tied to the desk
compensation.notes: Chloe does not want another discretionary bonus, which she described as a black box.

crm_note.notice_and_non_compete: Twelve weeks notice and six months non-compete. Bea asked about it and said this is standard for Brackenvane, they would cover it and they are used to it. Chloe had been worried it would stop the process.
competing_processes: First round done at a market maker in Amsterdam; Chloe said it is too early to say
risks: Bonus structure: Chloe wants a bonus tied to the desk and said she does not want another discretionary bonus. Brackenvane's bonus structure was not discussed.

next_actions.action: Speak to Brackenvane for feedback on the second round
Brackenvane to come back with the outcome of the second round

candidate.subject: Brackenvane second round: next steps
candidate.body:
Hi Chloe,

Thank you for talking me through the second round at Brackenvane Trading today, covering the mental maths test, the market-making and betting games and the options questions.

As I said on the call, I will speak to Brackenvane tomorrow about their feedback. They told you they would come back quickly, and if it goes well the final round would be with the head of the desk, focused on fit, possibly with a day on the desk.

For my notes, I have your current package as a base of £95k and a bonus of about £40k, and your expectation as a base of around £110k with a bonus tied to the desk rather than discretionary. It was good to hear that Bea said your twelve weeks notice and six month non-compete are standard for them.

Best wishes,
Hannah

client.subject: Chloe Adeyemi: second round feedback
client.body:

process.format: A mental maths test on a tablet (eighty questions in eight minutes), then a market-making game of about an hour. This includes a dice market, a second betting game on sizing, and options knowledge questions at the end.
process.who: Two traders from the index options desk, Sam and Bea
process.what_they_look_for: Fast, accurate arithmetic. Sensible quoting that adjusts as information is revealed, including widening when the other side trades as if informed. Always knowing your position. Sound bet sizing, including use of the Kelly criterion. Core options knowledge.

process.format: Described as more about how you would fit in, possibly with a day on the desk watching

examples: Eighty questions in eight minutes on a tablet, covering fractions, decimals and percentages
Make a market on the sum of three dice, with the interviewers trading against you and revealing dice one at a time
A betting game where you are offered bets at different odds and must decide sizing
Questions on the Kelly criterion and using it for sizing
What happens to a call's delta as expiry gets close
Why an index skew exists at all

went_well: In the dice game, widening the quote after being lifted a couple of times drew a question from Sam on why. The explanation was that the interviewers were trading as if they had information and the aim was not to keep getting picked off. Sam said "good" and added that a lot of people just keep quoting tight to look confident.
tripped_people_up: When Bea asked for the current position during the game, the answer was wrong by one lot. She said firmly: "always know your position".
In the betting game, sizing was kept too small. When Kelly came up, the criterion was known but not applied properly.
advice: For the second round, practise rapid mental arithmetic with fractions, decimals and percentages against the clock, since the test is eighty questions in eight minutes.
In the dice game, start from fair value, move your mid as dice are revealed, and widen if the interviewers keep trading against you. Be ready to explain why you widened.
Keep a running count of your position throughout the game so you can answer instantly when asked.
Practise applying the Kelly criterion to bets at different odds, so you can size properly rather than just state the formula.
Revise put-call parity, how a call's delta behaves near expiry, and why index skew exists, as these were asked at the end of the second round.
logistics: The second-round mental maths test is taken on a tablet before the market-making game.
The second-round market-making game lasts about an hour.
Notice period and non-compete are asked about in the second round. Bea asked about them.
Your record shows a 12-week notice period and a 6-month non-compete. Expect to be asked about these in the second round.
The final is with the head of the desk and may include a day on the desk watching.
